subject: Avoiding dotplots squished to bottom of plot

messages.author: bcb52a2d8001a6d1
messages.subject: Avoiding dotplots squished to bottom of plot
parts:
Thanks for a great product.  I am really enjoying using the new 0.9 features.

In dotplots, how do I avoid the plots squished to the bottom of the plots?  I have tried playing with limits in scale_y_continuous to no avail.

d<-data.frame(ppt=rep(c('a','b'),each=6),
val=c(1,1,1,1,1,1,1,1,2,2,3,3))
print(ggplot(d, aes(x=val))
+geom_dotplot()
+facet_wrap(~ppt)
+scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,.1)))

In other plots, it appears as if 60 dots are in fact 1.

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: Avoiding dotplots squished to bottom of plot
parts: As Ben noted, one way is to use 'dotsize', which changes the diameter of the dots... You can also use 'stackratio', which changes the vertical spacing between the dots:

ggplot(d, aes(x=val)) +
  geom_dotplot(stackratio=2) +
  facet_wrap(~ppt)

Unfortunately, for geom_dotplot, the numbers on the y axis are pretty much meaningless and I don't think it's possible to change this. If you want the dots to line up with actual count values, you have to tweak the y range by hand.

-Winston
